The streaming tar archiver builds each member's 512-byte ustar header from the
size it is told up front, then copies exactly that many bytes straight through
from the shared input stream. Because the length is known before the bytes, no
file is ever buffered whole -- the archiver, the gzip compressor, and the caller
all work a chunk at a time.

This file exists so the cli-tgz-maker example has something with a few hundred
bytes of real text to compress. Repetition compresses well, which makes the
gzip step visibly smaller than the raw tar:

  the quick brown fox jumps over the lazy dog
  the quick brown fox jumps over the lazy dog
  the quick brown fox jumps over the lazy dog
